---
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
{Bialgebras and Hopf Algebras}{hopf-alg}
  A graded \textbf{bialgebra} $B$ is a graded $k$-algebra with linear maps $\Delta: B \rightarrow B \otimes B$ and $\varepsilon: B \rightarrow k$  (called the \textbf{comultiplication} (or coproduct) and \textbf{counit}, respectively) such that
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item $\Delta$ and $\varepsilon$ are graded algebra homorphisms of degree zero.
  \end{enumerate}
  A graded \textbf{Hopf algebra} is a bialgebra $H$ along with a degree zero graded linear map $S: H \to H$ (called the \textbf{antipode}) such that
  \begin{equation*}
   \eta \circ \varepsilon(x) = \sum x_{(1)} S(x_{(2)}) = \sum S(x_{(1)}) x_{(2)}.
  \end{equation*}
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
{Grouplike Elements and Primitive Elements}{grouplike-primitive}
Let $B$ be a bialgebra. An element $g \in B$ is called \emph{grouplike} if it has the comultiplication
\begin{align*}
\Delta g = g \otimes g, \quad g \ne 0.
\end{align*}
An element $p \in B$ is called \emph{primitive} if
\begin{align*}
\Delta p = 1 \otimes p + p \otimes 1.
\end{align*}
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
{Properties of Grouplike and Primitive Elements}{•}
Let $B$ be a bialgebra.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The grouplike elements of $B$ form a monoid. Furthermore, if $B$ is a Hopf algebra with antipode $S$, the monoid of grouplike elements is a group, where the inverse of $g$ is $S(g)$.

\item The primitive elements of $B$ form a Lie algebra under the commutator bracket. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
{Hopf Algebra: Group Algebra}{hopf-group-alg}

  Let $G$ be a group (finite or infinite) and $k$ be a field. The group algebra $kG$ has the structure of a Hopf algebra with
  \begin{equation}
\begin{split}
\Delta g &= g \otimes g \\
\varepsilon(g) &= 1 \\
S(g) &= g^{-1}.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
for all $x \in G$.
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- example-2: body_md -->
{Hopf Algebra: Universal Enveloping Algebra}{hopf-universal-envel}
Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a Lie algebra. The universal enveloping algebra $U(\mathfrak{g})$ has the structure of a Hopf algebra with
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
\Delta x &= x \otimes 1 + 1 \otimes x \\
\varepsilon(x) &= 0 \\
S(x) &= -x.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
for all $x \in \mathfrak{g}$.
<!-- end example-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
{$*$-ring}{}
A \emph{$*$-ring} is a ring $R$ with an involution $*: R \to R$ such that
\begin{align*}
(x + y)^* &= x^* + y^* \\
(xy)^* &= y^* x^* \\
1^* &= 1,
\end{align*}
for all $x, y \in R$.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
{Graded $*$-Algebra}{}
A \emph{graded $*$-algebra} is a graded $k$-algebra $A$ with an involution \\ $*: A \to A$ such that 
\begin{align*}
(\alpha x + \beta y)^* &= \alpha^* x^* + \beta^* y^* \\
(xy)^* &= x^* y^*,
\end{align*}
for all $x,y \in A$ and $\alpha, \beta \in k$.
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- example-3: body_md -->
{Graded $*$-Algebra: Graded Algebra}{}
Every algebra $A$ over an ordinary (trivially starred) commutative ring has a trivial involution $x^* = x$ for all $x \in A$. Thus we can view every algebra as a $*$-algebra according to our definition.
<!-- end example-3 -->
<!-- example-4: body_md -->
{Graded $*$-algebra: Complex Matrices with Entrywise Conjugation}{}

Let $M_{n}(\mathbb{C})$ be the algebra of $n \times n$ complex matrices, and take as involution the entrywise conjugation of matrices. This defines a $*$-algebra in our sense.
<!-- end example-4 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
{Graded Frobenius Algebra}{}
A graded \emph{Frobenius $*$-algebra} $(F, \left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle)$, is a graded not necessarily associative algebra $F$ over a $*$-ring $k$, with non-degenerate bilinear form $\left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle: F \otimes F \to k$, such that
\begin{equation}
\left\langle xy,z \right\rangle = \left\langle x,y z \right\rangle
\end{equation}
for all $x,y,z \in F$, and such that for all non-zero $x \in F$, there exist some $a,b \in F$ with $a x \ne 0$ and $x b \ne 0$. We do not assume that F is unital nor finite-dimensional.
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
{}{frob-2-pairings}
Let $F$ be a graded Frobenius $*$-algebra with bilinear form $\left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle_{\text{Frob}}$. Then there is an associated sesquilinear form $\left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle$, defined by 
\begin{equation}
\left\langle x,y \right\rangle \equiv \left\langle x,y^* \right\rangle_{\text{Frob}}
\end{equation}
which satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sesq-assoc}
\left\langle xy, z \right\rangle = \left\langle x,y^* z \right\rangle.
\end{equation}
Similarly, given a sesequilinear form on $F$, $\left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle$, satisfying \Cref{eq:sesq-assoc}, there is an associated bilinear form $\left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle_{\text{Frob}}$ that gives $F$ the structure of a Frobenius algebra, defined by
\begin{equation}
\left\langle x,y \right\rangle_{\text{Frob}} \equiv \left\langle x, y^* \right\rangle.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
{}{frob-unital-counit}
Let $F$ be an \textbf{associative} unital graded Frobenius algebra. Then there is a linear functional $\varepsilon: F \to k$ whose kernel contains no non-trivial ideals (left nor right), such that 
\begin{equation}
\left\langle x,y \right\rangle = \varepsilon(xy^*).
\end{equation}
Conversely, given any non-zero functional $\varepsilon$ with simple kernel on an associative algebra, $\left\langle x,y \right\rangle = \varepsilon(xy^*)$ defines a (sesquilinear) Frobenius form.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- example-5: body_md -->
{Frobenius $*$-Algebra: $n \times n$ Matrices}{frb-matrices-with-conj}

  Let $(M_{n}(\mathbb{C}), *)$ be the $*$-algebra of $n \times n$ matrices with entrywise conjugation. We define our bilinear form as
  \begin{equation*}
   \left\langle A,B \right\rangle_{\text{Frob}} = \operatorname{Tr}(A B^{T}).
  \end{equation*}
The corresponding sesquilinear pairing is then the ordinary inner product of matrices:
\begin{equation*}
 \left\langle A,B \right\rangle = \operatorname{Tr}(A B^{\dagger}).
\end{equation*}
<!-- end example-5 -->
<!-- example-6: body_md -->
{Frobenius $*$-Algebra: Composition Algebras}{comp-alg}
A \emph{composition algebra} is a finite-dimensional vector space $V$ with not necessarily associative multiplication, a unit, and a non-degenerate symmetric bilinear form $(\cdot, \cdot)$, such that 
\begin{equation}
(xy, xy) = (x,x) (y,y).
\end{equation}
<!-- end example-6 -->
<!-- example-7: body_md -->
{Frobenius Algebra: Euclidean Space}{frb-euclid}

  Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real vector space and choose a basis $\{ e_i \}$. We can give $V$ the structure of a Frobenius algebra with multiplication
  \begin{equation*}
   e_i e_j = \delta_{ij}e_j
  \end{equation*}
  and pairing
  \begin{equation*}
   \left\langle e_i, e_j \right\rangle = \delta_{ij}
  \end{equation*}
  where $\delta_{ij}$ is the Kronecker delta.
<!-- end example-7 -->
<!-- example-8: body_md -->
{Real Frobenius $*$-Algebra: Complex Numbers}{frb-complex}
                                                                
Consider the real vector space $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, with basis $\{ a_i, b_i \}_{i=1}^n$. We impose the following multiplication
\begin{align*}
a_i b_j &= \delta_{ij} b_i \\
b_i a_j &= \delta_{ij} b_i \\
a_i a_j &= \delta_{ij} a_i \\
b_i b_j &= -\delta_{ij} a_i,
\end{align*}
take the counit to be $\varepsilon(a_i) = 1$, $\varepsilon(b_i) = 1$, and let the star involution be $a_i^* = a_i$, $b_i^* = - b_i$.
<!-- end example-8 -->
<!-- example-9: body_md -->
{Real Frobenius $*$-Algebra: Orthogonal Form}{frb-orthog}
Take the same $*$-algebra structure on $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ as in the previous example, but consider the following counit:
\begin{align*}
\varepsilon_O(a_i) &= 1 \\
\varepsilon_O(b_i) &= 0.
\end{align*}
The Frobenius form in this example is the standard orthogonal form on $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$.
<!-- end example-9 -->
<!-- example-10: body_md -->
{Real Frobenius $*$-Algebra: Symplectic Form}{frb-symp}
If we take the same $*$-algebra structure on $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ as in the previous two examples, but select our counit to be 
\begin{align*}
\varepsilon_S(a_i) &= 0 \\
\varepsilon_S(b_i) &= 1
\end{align*}
our Frobenius form becomes the standard symplectic form.
<!-- end example-10 -->
<!-- example-11: body_md -->
{Frobenius Algebra: Hilbert Space with Basis}{frb-hilbert}
                                                                
Let $H$ be a Hilbert space (even one that is non-separable). Pick an orthonormal basis $\{ e_\alpha \}$ and define a multiplication as follows: given any two elements $x = \sum_{i=1}^{\infty} x_{\alpha_i} e_{\alpha_i}$, $y = \sum_{j=1}^{\infty} y_{\beta_j} e_{\beta_j}$, let 
\begin{align*}
xy \equiv \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} x_{\gamma_k} y_{\gamma_k} e_{\gamma_k},
\end{align*}
where $\{ e_{\gamma_k} \}_{k=1}^{\infty} = \{ e_{\alpha_i} \}_{i=1}^{\infty} \cup \{ e_{\beta_j} \}_{j=1}^{\infty}$, and the coefficients $x_i, y_j$ have been reindexed appropriately. With the pairing
 
\begin{align*}
\left\langle x,y \right\rangle_{\text{Frob}} \equiv \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} x_{\gamma_k} y_{\gamma_k},
\end{align*}
this has the structure of a Frobenius algebra. For more information on non-separable Hilbert spaces, see \cite{martin-book}.
<!-- end example-11 -->
<!-- example-12: body_md -->
{Frobenius Algebra: Compactly Supported Functions}{frb-comp-supp}
                                                                
Let $C_c^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ be the algebra of smooth compactly supported functions. The pairing
\begin{equation}
\left\langle f,g \right\rangle_{\text{Frob}} = \int f g
\end{equation}
gives $C_c^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ the structure of a Frobenius algebra.
<!-- end example-12 -->
<!-- example-13: body_md -->
{Frobenius Algebra: Schwartz Space}{frb-schwartz}
                                                                
Let 
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{S} = \{ f \in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n, \mathbb{C}) \mid \forall \alpha, \beta, \sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}^n} \lvert x_1^{\alpha_1} \ldots x_n^{\alpha_n} (\partial_1^{\beta_1} \ldots \partial_n^{\beta_n} f) \rvert < \infty \}
\end{align*}
be the algebra of Schwartz functions. The pairing
\begin{equation}
\left\langle f,g \right\rangle = \int f g^*
\end{equation}
gives $\mathcal{S}$ the structure of a Frobenius $*$-algebra.
<!-- end example-13 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
{Hopf-Frobenius Module}{hf-mod}
A \emph{left Hopf-Frobenius module} is a pair $(H,F)$ where $H$ is a (graded) Hopf algebra, and $F$ is a (graded) Frobenius algebra such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F$ has the structure of a left $H$-module.

\item $\sum (-1)^{\lvert x \rvert \lvert g_{(2)} \rvert} \left\langle g_{(1)} x, g_{(2)} y \right\rangle = \varepsilon_H(g) \left\langle x,y \right\rangle$.

\item $\left\langle g x, y \right\rangle = (-1)^{\lvert g \rvert \lvert x \rvert} \left\langle x, S(g) y \right\rangle $ 
\end{enumerate}
for all $g \in H$ and $x,y \in F$.
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
{}{}
Let $H$ be a Hopf algebra and $F$ be Frobenius algebras which is also a left $H$-module. If $H$ and $F$ satisfy
\begin{align*}
\sum (-1)^{\lvert x \rvert \lvert g_{(2)} \rvert} \left\langle g_{(1)} x, g_{(2)} y \right\rangle &= \varepsilon_H(g) \left\langle x,y \right\rangle
\end{align*}
and $g$ is grouplike or primitive, then $\left\langle S(g) x,y \right\rangle = (-1)^{\lvert g \rvert \lvert x \rvert} \left\langle x,gy \right\rangle$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
{}{}
Let $H$ be a Hopf algebra and $F$ be a Frobenius algebra that is also a left $H$-module. If $g,h \in H$ satisfy 
\begin{align*}
\sum (-1)^{\lvert x \rvert \lvert g_{(2)} \rvert} \left\langle g_{(1)} x, g_{(2)} y \right\rangle = \varepsilon_H(g) \left\langle x,y \right\rangle
\end{align*}
for all $x,y \in F$ then so does the product $gh$. Similarly, if $g,h$ satisfy
\begin{align*}
\left\langle g x, y \right\rangle = (-1)^{\lvert g \rvert \lvert x \rvert} \left\langle x, S(g) y \right\rangle
\end{align*}
for all $x,y$, 
then so does $gh$.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
{Frobenius Algebra Topology is Induced from Vector Space Basis}{frob-top-basis}
Let $F$ be a vector space with bilinear form $\left\langle -,- \right\rangle$, and $B = \{ b_i \}$ be any basis and let 
\begin{align*}
X_F &= \{ \left\langle -,x \right\rangle, \left\langle x,- \right\rangle \mid x \in F \} \\
X_B &= \{ \left\langle -, b_i \right\rangle, \left\langle b_i, - \right\rangle \mid b_i \in B \}.
\end{align*}
If $\tau_F$ is the initial topology on $F$ induced by the maps in $X_F$ and $\tau_B$ is the initial topology induced by $X_B$, then
\begin{align*}
\tau_B = \tau_F.
\end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
{}{bilinear-cont-at-zero}
Let $V,W$ be topological vector spaces. Then a bilinear map $\left\langle -,- \right\rangle: V_1 \times V_2 \to W$ is continuous if and only if it is continuous at $(0,0)$.
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
{Finite-Dimensional Frobenius Algebra Pairings are Jointly Continuous}{frob-jointly-cont}
Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional Frobenius algebra, viewed as a topological vector space with topology induced from $\left\langle x,- \right\rangle_{\text{Frob}}, \left\langle -,y \right\rangle_{\text{Frob}}$. Then the pairing
\begin{align*}
\left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle_{\text{Frob}}: F \times F \to k
\end{align*}
is jointly continuous. Similarly, if $F$ is over a trivially-starred field, and we give $F$ the topology induced by $\left\langle x,- \right\rangle, \left\langle -,y \right\rangle$, then
\begin{align*}
\left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle: F \times F \to k
\end{align*}
is jointly continuous.
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
{Hopf-Frobenius Modules Can be Pulled Back}{}
Let $(H,F)$ be a Hopf-Frobenius module, let $G$ be a (graded) Hopf algebra, and let $\phi: G \rightarrow H$ be a (graded) Hopf algebra homomorphism (of degree zero). Then $(G, \phi^{*} F)$ is a Hopf-Frobenius module, where $\phi^{*} F = F$ is restriction of scalars on the module $F$, viewed as a $G$-module:
\begin{equation*}
 g \cdot x = \phi(g) \cdot x,
\end{equation*}
for all $g \in G$ and $x \in F$.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- example-14: body_md -->
{HF-Module: Trivial Hopf Action}{}
  Let $F$ be any Frobenius algebra and let $H$ be any Hopf algebra, both over the field $k$. Then there is a trivial Hopf-Frobenius module structure on $(H,F)$ given by pulling back the counit
\begin{equation*}
\varepsilon : H \rightarrow k.
\end{equation*}
Explicitly, $h \cdot f = \varepsilon(h) f$ for all $h \in H$, $f \in F$.
<!-- end example-14 -->
<!-- example-15: body_md -->
{HF-Module: Lie Groups}{}
Let $O(n)$ be the orthogonal group, and take $F = \mathbb{R}^n$ with the standard basis and let $H = \mathbb{R} O(n)$ be the group algebra of the orthogonal group. Letting $O(n)$ act on $F$ by its standard representation and extending to $H$ linearly, gives an HF-module.
<!-- end example-15 -->
<!-- example-16: body_md -->
{HF-Module: Lie Algebras}{}
Let $\mathfrak{o}(n) = \mathfrak{so}(n)$ be the orthogonal Lie algebra (i.e. the skew-symmetric matrices) and take our Hopf algebra to be the universal enveloping algebra $U[\mathfrak{o}(n)]$. Let $F = \mathbb{R}^n$ with the standard basis. Let $\mathfrak{o}(n)$ act on $F$ by its standard representation and extend to $H$ by letting products of elements of $\mathfrak{o}(n)$ act on $F$ by composition. This has the structure of an HF-module.
<!-- end example-16 -->
<!-- example-17: body_md -->
{HF-Module: Schwartz Space with Derivatives}{}

Let $F = \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ be Schwartz space as in \Cref{ex:frb-schwartz} and $H = \mathbb{R}[\partial_1, \ldots, \partial_n]$ be a polynomial algebra whose action on $F$ is given by partial derivatives. Then $(H,F)$ is a Hopf-Frobenius module.
<!-- end example-17 -->
<!-- example-18: body_md -->
{HF-Module: Compactly Supported Functions with Derivations}{}
Let $M$ be an orientable smooth $n$-manifold equipped with a volume form $\omega \in \Omega^n(M)$. Take as Frobenius algebra $F = C^{\infty}_c(M)$ as in \Cref{ex:frb-comp-supp}. Consider the Lie algebra of derivations $\operatorname{Der}(C^{\infty}_c(M))$, which is isomorphic to the Lie algebra of vector fields $\mathfrak{X}(M)$, which acts on $C^{\infty}_c(M)$. Let $H = U[\operatorname{Der}(C^{\infty}_c(M))]$ be the universal enveloping algebra on the derivations so that $F$ is a left $H$-module. The pair $(H,F)$ is a Hopf-Frobenius module.
<!-- end example-18 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
{}{}
Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff topological group and consider the group Hopf algebra $H = kG$. Let $F = C_c(G)$ be the algebra of compactly supported functions on $G$, and give $F$ the structure of a left $H$-module by $C_c(G)$ by $g \cdot \phi(h) = \phi (hg)$. Then given any measure $\mu$ on $G$ such that the linear functional
\begin{equation}
\varepsilon_\mu(\phi) = \int \phi d\mu
\end{equation}
has a simple kernel, $(H,F)$ is a Hopf-Frobenius module if and only if $\mu$ is a Haar measure.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
{}{lie-alg-for-grouplike}
Let $G$ be a group and consider the group algebra $kG$. The vector subspace of $kG$ generated by 
\begin{equation}
\{ g - g^{-1} \mid g \in G \}
\end{equation}
is a Lie algebra under the commutator bracket.
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
{Lie Algebra of a Hopf Algebra}{lie-alg-of-hopf}
Let $H$ be a Hopf algebra and consider the vector subspace generated by
\begin{equation}
\{ x - S(x) \mid x \in H \text{ and } S^{2}(x) = x \}.
\end{equation}
This is a Lie algebra under the commutator bracket.
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
{Lie Algebra of a Hopf Algebra}{}
Let $H$ be a Hopf algebra. The \emph{Lie algebra associated to $H$} is the vector space
\begin{equation*}
\mathfrak{L}_H \equiv \{ \sum_i \alpha_i (x - S(x)) \mid x \in H, S^2(x) = x, \alpha_i \in k \},
\end{equation*}
with the commutator bracket.
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
{}{}
Let $\mathfrak{L}: \textsc{Gr} \to \textsc{L.Alg}$ be the assignment from the category of groups to the category of Lie algebras which sends $G$ to $\mathfrak{L}_G$ and $\phi: G \to H$ to the morphism $\mathfrak{L}_\phi$ defined by 
\begin{equation*}
\mathfrak{L}_\phi(g - g^{-1}) = \phi(g) - \phi(g)^{-1}.
\end{equation*}
This is a functor.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
{}{lie-alg-matches}
Let $G$ be a Lie group over a field $k$ that satisfies the following property: 

\begin{enumerate}
\item There exists a finite collection of non-degenerate bilinear forms $\left\langle -,- \right\rangle_{i}$ on a vector space $V$ such that $G = \{ g \in \operatorname{End}(V) \mid \left\langle g x, gy \right\rangle_i = \left\langle x,y \right\rangle_i$ for all $i \}$, and the Lie algebra of $G$ is $\mathfrak{g} = \{ A \in \operatorname{End}(V) \mid \left\langle Ax, y \right\rangle_i = - \left\langle x, Ay \right\rangle_i $ for all $i \}$.
\end{enumerate}

Then $\mathfrak{L}_G \cong \mathfrak{g}$.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- example-19: body_md -->
{Lie Groups Satisfying \Cref{prop:lie-alg-matches}}{}

This class of Lie groups and Lie algebras covers a wide range, including most of the classical Lie groups/algebras: $O(n)$, $U(n)$, $Sp(2n)$, $O(p,q)$ (the indefinite orthogonal group), and in particular, the Lorentz group $\Lambda = O(1,3)$.
<!-- end example-19 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
{}{lie-alg-matches-gl-sl}
Let $G$ be $GL(n)$ or $SL(n)$ over a field $k$ with $\operatorname{char}(k) \ne 2$, with corresponding Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$. Then
\begin{equation*}
\mathfrak{L}_G \cong \mathfrak{g}.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
{The Group Generated by Primitive Elements}{lie-group-of-hopf}
Let $H$ be a Hopf algebra. Let $F$ be an algebra which is not necessarily unital nor associative, and which is a left $H$-module. And let $\{ \left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle_i \}_{i \in I}$ be finitely many bilinear forms which each give $F$ the structure of a Frobenius algebra and turn $(H,F)$ into a Hopf-Frobenius module (for the same fixed action by $H$). Let $P$ be the primitive elements of $H$. Let $U = U[P]$ be the subalgebra generated by $P$ and consider the induced action of $U[P]$ on $F$. Then
\begin{align*}
U[P]_F \equiv \{ g \in U/\operatorname{ann} F \mid &\left\langle g x, gy \right\rangle_i = \left\langle S(g) x, S(g) y \right\rangle_i = \left\langle x,y \right\rangle_i \\
 &\text{ and } \left\langle S(g) x, y \right\rangle_i = \left\langle x, g y \right\rangle_i \text{ for all } i \}
\end{align*}
forms a group, where $g^{-1} = S(g)$. Here  $\operatorname{ann} F \subseteq U$ denotes the annihilator of $F$ with respect to the $U$-module structure.
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- definition-8: body_md -->
{Lie Group of a Hopf-Frobenius Module}{lie-group-hf-mod}
Let $(H,F, \{ \left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle_i \}_{i \in I})$ be as above and let $U$ be the subalgebra generated by the primitive elements of $H$. We denote the group constructed above by
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{G}^H_F \equiv \{ g \in U/\operatorname{ann} F \mid &\left\langle g x, gy \right\rangle_i = \left\langle S(g) x, S(g) y \right\rangle = \left\langle x,y \right\rangle_i \\
 &\text{ and } \left\langle S(g) x, y \right\rangle_i = \left\langle x, g y \right\rangle_i, \text{ for all } i \}
\end{align*}
and call it the \emph{Lie group of $(H,F, \{ \left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle_i \}_{i \in I})$}.
<!-- end definition-8 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
{}{lie-group-gives-hfm}
Let $(H,F, \{ \left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle_i \}_{i \in I})$ be a Hopf-Frobenius module. Then $(k \mathcal{G}_F^H, F, \{ \left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle_i \}_{i \in I})$ is also a Hopf-Frobenius module.
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
{}{antipode-cont}
Let $(H,F, \{ \left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle_i \}_{i \in I})$ be a Hopf-Frobenius module with Lie group $\mathcal{G}^H_F$, where $F$ is given the topology induced by all $\left\langle x,- \right\rangle_i, \left\langle -,y \right\rangle_i$. Give $\mathcal{G}^H_F$ the initial topology induced by the maps
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{G}^H_F \xrightarrow{- \cdot x} F
\end{equation}
for all $x \in F$. Then the antipode map $S: \mathcal{G}^H_F \to \mathcal{G}^H_F$ is continuous.
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
{}{action-cont}
Let $(H,F, \{ \left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle_i \}_{i \in I})$ be a Hopf-Frobenius module where $F$ is finite-dimensional and over a trivially-starred field. Then the action of $\mathcal{G}_F^H$ on $F$
\begin{align*}
- \cdot - : \mathcal{G}_F^H \times F \to F
\end{align*}
is jointly continuous.
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
{The Lie Group of an HF-Module is a Topological Group}{top-group}
Let $(H,F, \{ \left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle_i \}_{i \in I})$ be a Hopf-Frobenius module where $F$ is finite-dimensional and over a trivially-starred field. The initial topology induced by the maps
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{G}^H_F \xrightarrow{- \cdot x} F
\end{equation}
for all $x \in F$ gives $\mathcal{G}^H_F$ the structure of a topological group.
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
{}{filtration-gives-endo}
Let $\rho: \mathcal{A} \to \operatorname{End}(V)$ be a finite-dimensional faithful irreducible representation of a unital associative algebra over a field $k$ such that there is a filtration of the form
\begin{equation*}
\rho(A_m \ldots A_1)(V) \subseteq \rho(A_{m-1} \ldots A_1)(V) \subseteq \ldots \subseteq \rho(A_1)(V) \subseteq V
\end{equation*}
where $A_i \in \mathcal{A}$ and $\dim \rho(A_m \ldots A_1)(V) = 1$. Then
\begin{equation}
\rho(\mathcal{A}) \cong \operatorname{End}(V).
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
{}{lie-groups-that-work}
Let $G$ be one of the following Lie groups with its standard representation:
\begin{align*}
\{ O(n), SO(n) \mid n > 2 \} \cup \{ Sp(n), O(m,n) \}.
\end{align*}
Then the induced representation of the universal enveloping algebra $U[\mathfrak{g}]$ surjects onto $\operatorname{End}(V)$ for the corresponding $V$.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
{}{unitary-surj}
Let $G = U(n)$ with $n \geq 2$ or $SU(n)$ with $n > 2$ and consider the Hopf-Frobenius module given by $\mathbb{R} G$ acting on $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$. By abuse of notation, let $\operatorname{End}(\mathbb{C}^{n})$ be the subspace of $\operatorname{End}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ identified with complex matrices.Then $U[\mathfrak{u}(n)]$ surjects onto $\operatorname{End}(\mathbb{C}^{n})$.
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
{}{lie-group-matches-topologically}
Let $G$ be one of the following Lie groups: $Sp(\mathbb{R}^{2n}, \mathbb{R})$, $\{ U(n) \mid n \geq 2 \}$, or $\{ O(n) \mid n > 2 \}$, and let $\rho: G \to GL(F)$ be its standard representation on the corresponding vector space $F$ with bilinear forms $\{ \left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle_i \}_{i \in I}$. In particular, the action of $G$ preserves the forms:
\begin{equation*}
\left\langle gx,gy \right\rangle_i = \left\langle x,y \right\rangle_i, \text{ for all } g \in G, x,y \in F, i \in I.
\end{equation*}
If $\mathfrak{g}$ is the Lie algebra of $G$ and $U[\mathfrak{g}]$ is its universal enveloping algebra then
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{G}_F^{U[\mathfrak{g}]} \cong G
\end{equation*}
as topological groups.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
